selected_evidence.requirement: HAProxy serves HTTP on port 80 and forwards to the loopback-only Node.js backend
selected_evidence.summary: Before and after reboot, port 80 listened on all interfaces, port 3000 listened only on 127.0.0.1, and both frontend and backend returned HTTP 200 with exact body `infraset-nodejs`.
Shows the named service running its Node.js process and remaining active and enabled across reboot.
HAProxy syntax validation succeeded during configuration and after reboot.

Healthy baseline used boot ID ac73b359-243e-418e-b7bb-a7cff423e597; restart was acknowledged; node returned with changed boot ID 992ab083-fd34-440b-90b4-53d72869e0c0; both services, listeners, configuration, and HTTP responses recovered.

commands.command:
set -eu
sudo tee /etc/systemd/system/infraset-nodejs.service >/dev/null <<'ANTRIEB_UNIT_EOF'
[Unit]
Description=InfraSet Node.js application
After=network.target

[Service]
Type=simple
User=infraset-nodejs
Group=infraset-nodejs
ExecStart=/usr/bin/nodejs /opt/infraset-nodejs/server.js
Restart=on-failure
RestartSec=2
NoNewPrivileges=true
PrivateTmp=true

[Install]
WantedBy=multi-user.target
ANTRIEB_UNIT_EOF
sudo tee -a /etc/haproxy/haproxy.cfg >/dev/null <<'ANTRIEB_HAPROXY_EOF'

frontend infraset_http
    bind *:80
    default_backend infraset_nodejs

backend infraset_nodejs
    server nodejs 127.0.0.1:3000 check
ANTRIEB_HAPROXY_EOF
sudo systemctl daemon-reload
sudo haproxy -c -f /etc/haproxy/haproxy.cfg
printf 'configuration-valid\n'

set -eu
sudo systemctl enable infraset-nodejs.service
sudo systemctl start infraset-nodejs.service
for i in 1 2 3 4 5; do systemctl is-active --quiet infraset-nodejs.service && break; sleep 1; done
systemctl is-active infraset-nodejs.service
systemctl is-enabled infraset-nodejs.service
ss -ltnp | awk 'NR == 1 || /:3000[[:space:]]/'
printf 'direct_body='; curl -fsS http://127.0.0.1:3000/; printf '\n'
